| `tps-floor` | 15.0 | 5..19.5 |
| `window-seconds` | 10 | 3..120 |

| `max-radius` | **48** | **1..64** |

| `status-log-seconds` | 300 | 30..3600 |

### 1b. The per-tick budget is all-or-nothing per call, not per tick
Quote from `NxPerfCore.java:71-84`:
```
71 public synchronized boolean take(long nowTick, int n) {
72   if (nowTick != tick) { tick = nowTick; used = 0; }
76   if (n <= 0) return true;
77   if ((long) used + n > perTick) { denied++; return false; }
81   used += n; total += n; return true;
```
- **Per call:** `take(name, n)` never grants part of `n`. If `used + n > perTick` it returns false and consumes nothing.
- **Over a tick:** callers that take 1 at a time (the usual `take(name)`) get partial progress until `used == perTick`, then every call returns false until the tick number changes.
- **One request larger than the budget is always refused.** `NxPerfCoreTest.java` line 20 checks `!b.take(3, 65)`. A model that calls `take("x", 100)` against a 64 budget will never run.
- **Each name has its own budget.** `NxPerf.java:299-303` creates a `Budget` per name via `computeIfAbsent`. The 64 is therefore per feature name, not plugin-wide, and a plugin can sidestep it by using many names.
- **Paused plugins get nothing.** `take` returns false when paused (`NxPerf.java:300`). `remaining` returns 0 when paused.
- **Tick source:** `Bukkit.getCurrentTick()`.
- **Queues:** `Queue.drain` (`NxPerf.java:395-414`) loops `while (!items.isEmpty() && take(name, 1))`. A queue stops at the budget and carries the rest to the next tick. `offer` drops when `items.size() >= maxQueue` or when paused, and logs "queue X is full" once (`:377-383`).
- **Spawns:** `spawnAllowed` (`:314-323`) gives a false when paused, or when the chunk already holds `maxEntitiesPerChunk` living non-player entities (counted live), or when the token bucket (`maxEntitiesPerSecond`, burst of one second's worth) is empty.

## 1. PERF LAYER

### 1a. Where the defaults are set
There are three copies, and they have to stay in sync.
- **Java defaults and clamps:** `services/modbuilder/perf/src/NxPerfCore.java:25-52` (`Settings`, `clampAll`).
- **Java config reader:** `NxPerf.java:97-117` (`readSettings`). Each `c.getX("perf.key", default)` call repeats the default.
- **Injected `config.yml` section:** `services/modbuilder/perf.js:21-35` (`CONFIG_SECTION`). It is appended only if the file has no `perf:` block (`perf.js:99`).

| Config key | Default | Clamp (Core:41-52) |
|---|---|---|
| `auto-disable` | true | none |
| `tps-floor` | 15.0 | 5..19.5 |
| `window-seconds` | 10 | 3..120 |
| `max-work-per-tick` | 64 | 1..256 |
| `max-ms-per-tick` | 25.0 | 2..45 |
| `share` | 0.25 | 0.05..0.9 |
| `freezeMs` | 2000 | 250..10000. Not read from config, so it is fixed at 2000. |
| `max-entities-per-second` | 5 | 1..50 |
| `max-entities-per-chunk` | 20 | 1..100 |
| `max-queue` | 2000 | 10..20000 |
| `max-radius` | **48** | **1..64** |
| `max-spawns-per-second` | 50 | 1..500 |
| `status-log-seconds` | 300 | 30..3600 |

- A config value can only tighten limits or loosen them up to these clamps. `Core:23` says "a config can tighten the limits, never remove them". A broken config keeps the defaults (`NxPerf.java:112-114`). Settings are re-read every 30 s (`NxPerf.java:149`).
- **The radius numbers disagree across files:** the default is 48 and the clamp is 64. `prompts.js` says "at most 48". `perf-risk.ts:227,270` says "hard maximum 48". `perf.js:202` flags a config radius above 64. The failure-rules line says 4 chunks. Only the Core clamp (64) is actually enforced.

### 1b. The per-tick budget is all-or-nothing per call, not per tick
Quote from `NxPerfCore.java:71-84`:
```
71 public synchronized boolean take(long nowTick, int n) {
72   if (nowTick != tick) { tick = nowTick; used = 0; }
76   if (n <= 0) return true;
77   if ((long) used + n > perTick) { denied++; return false; }
81   used += n; total += n; return true;
```
- **Per call:** `take(name, n)` never grants part of `n`. If `used + n > perTick` it returns false and consumes nothing.
- **Over a tick:** callers that take 1 at a time (the usual `take(name)`) get partial progress until `used == perTick`, then every call returns false until the tick number changes.
- **One request larger than the budget is always refused.** `NxPerfCoreTest.java` line 20 checks `!b.take(3, 65)`. A model that calls `take("x", 100)` against a 64 budget will never run.
- **Each name has its own budget.** `NxPerf.java:299-303` creates a `Budget` per name via `computeIfAbsent`. The 64 is therefore per feature name, not plugin-wide, and a plugin can sidestep it by using many names.
- **Paused plugins get nothing.** `take` returns false when paused (`NxPerf.java:300`). `remaining` returns 0 when paused.
- **Tick source:** `Bukkit.getCurrentTick()`.
- **Queues:** `Queue.drain` (`NxPerf.java:395-414`) loops `while (!items.isEmpty() && take(name, 1))`. A queue stops at the budget and carries the rest to the next tick. `offer` drops when `items.size() >= maxQueue` or when paused, and logs "queue X is full" once (`:377-383`).
- **Spawns:** `spawnAllowed` (`:314-323`) gives a false when paused, or when the chunk already holds `maxEntitiesPerChunk` living non-player entities (counted live), or when the token bucket (`maxEntitiesPerSecond`, burst of one second's worth) is empty.
- **Plugin-wide spawn guard:** `SpawnGuard` (`:225-237`) cancels any `EntitySpawnEvent` caused by the plugin's own code once `ownSpawnsSecond >= maxSpawnsPerSecond`, or while paused.
- **Radius:** `radius(int)` clamps to 1..`maxRadius` (`:345`).
- **Not forced at runtime:** the model has to call these APIs. The prompt and `perfcheck` push it to, but nothing stops code that skips them.

### 1c. Auto-disable and pause
`NxPerf.tick()` runs every tick (`:119-156`). Four triggers call `pause(reason, detail)` (only if `!paused && S.autoDisable`):
1. **freeze (`:122`):** one tick of the plugin's listener time is above 2000 ms.
2. **entities (`:136`):** spawns were denied in 3 consecutive seconds.
3. **tps / budget (`:139-141`):** `Judge.add` returns a verdict (`NxPerfCore.java:150-165`).
   - TPS verdict: for the whole window (default 10 s), TPS was under the floor (15) and the plugin's own ms per tick was at least 25% of the tick length.
   - BUDGET verdict: for the whole window, own ms per tick was above `max-ms-per-tick` (25), even if TPS held.
4. **manual:** `/<cmd> perf pause` (`:512`).

- **Low TPS with a small share is never a pause.** It logs `[NxPerf] LAG plugin=.. tps=.. own_ms=.. (not caused by this plugin)` once (`:142-144`).
- **What `pause` does (`:242-269`):**
  - Unregisters the plugin's costliest listeners until 90% of the measured listener cost is covered.
  - Stops all `NxPerf.timer`s, clears all queues, and runs `onPause` hooks.
  - Logs at WARNING: `[NxPerf] PAUSED plugin=<n> reason=<freeze|entities|tps|budget|manual> tps=.. own_ms=.. listeners=a,b timers=N detail=..`
  - Sends the ops a gold chat message: "Performance safety paused this mod's heavy features (...). The server keeps running. Check with /<label> perf status, resume with ... perf resume."
- **Resume:** manual only, via `perf resume`. It logs `[NxPerf] RESUMED plugin=.. by=..` and resets the judge. Nothing resumes it automatically.
- **Other log lines:**
  - Start: `[NxPerf] watchdog nxperf-1 on: pauses heavy features below 15.00 TPS for 10 s (perf.auto-disable=true)`.
  - Status: `[NxPerf] status v= plugin= tps= paper_tps= mspt= own_ms= spawns_denied= paused=`, every 30 s for the first 15 min, then every `status-log-seconds`.
- **Command access:** the `perf` command needs OP, the console, or the `<plugin>.perf` permission (`:504-509`).
- **Verdict:** `auto-disable: false` is allowed. Pause, throttling and the clamps are SOFTEN-able in values, but the watchdog itself, its injection and its log format are H (see below).

### 1d. Build-service enforcement (`services/modbuilder/perf.js`)
- **Injection (`:70-104`):** the watchdog sources are overwritten on every build, `NxPerf.init(this)` is inserted into `onEnable`, and imported plugins are skipped. `MB_PERF_SAFETY=0` turns it off. **H** (it keeps the model from shipping a modified watchdog).
- **`perfcheck` (`:141-188`) is advisory.** It reports `perf-world-iteration`, `perf-spawn-in-loop`, `perf-explosion-in-loop`, `perf-chunk-load-in-loop`, `perf-block-loop`, `perf-raw-timer`, `perf-call-event`, `perf-infinite-loop`, and `perf-huge-literal` (a nearby-entity radius of 3+ digits).
  - Findings go back to the model once (`server.js:1033`) and are recorded as "warn" findings that never block (`server.js:1270`).
  - **S** as a whole. `perf-infinite-loop` is arguably crash prevention but still only warns.
- **`configCheck` (`:190-206`):**

| Rule | Condition | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `perf-config-per-tick` | a per-tick, batch or per-cycle key above **256** | sent back to the model |
| `perf-config-radius` | radius, range or distance above **64** (excluding view, chat, teleport, border and similar keys) | sent back to the model |
| `perf-config-mob-copy` | mirror or copy mobs set to true | sent back to the model |

  - All three are **S** (a user could be allowed to exceed them with a warning).

### 1e. Prompt and sheet text that tells the AI the limits
- **`services/modbuilder/prompts.js:36-48`, `PERF_SECTION`, "hard rule 10":**
  - Radius via `NxPerf.radius(<configured radius>)`, "at most 48 blocks".
  - Per tick: "at most perf.max-work-per-tick ... (default 64)".
  - Spawning: 5 per second, 20 living mobs per chunk, copy generations at most 3.
  - Explosions: `rate("explosions", 5)` and power at most 4.
  - Timers: a period of 10 ticks or more.
  - Safe config defaults: "radius 16, per-tick 64 or less, mob copying off", clamped with `Math.min`.
  - "If the request asks for unbounded work ... build the bounded version ... and say so in modbuilder.json limitations". This sentence is the main thing that turns a user's number into a clamp. **S** (soften it to "warn, and honour the number up to the clamp").
- **`services/modbuilder/rules/failure-rules.json:383`:** the ChunkMirror lesson. It says at most 4 chunks, a queue at most `perf.max-work-per-tick` per tick, and mob copying off.
- **`services/modbuilder/sheets/*.md`** contain no perf text. The grep hit only a gamerule line.
- **Appended to every build while the switch is on:** `PERF_SECTION` is added to every generated build's system prompt (`prompts.js:36,50`).

### 1f. TS side (`lib/cyrus/safety`)
- **`perf-caps.ts`** (all 8 perf rules R1-R8 over the designer, boss, HUD, motion, datapack and worldgen constants):
  - It only builds a table, "nothing here is enforced at runtime" (`:8`).

  - **Not wired in this branch:** the only importer is `testflight/stress.ts` (for `perfSafetyEnabled`). `classifyPerfRisk`, `perfPreBuildCheck` and `applyPerfChoice` are called from nowhere but tests. The comment (`:7`) says it is for the planner on "another branch".

## Summary of the softening picture
- **Already a warning or a choice:** `perfcheck` and `configCheck` (never block), the `perf-risk` "safe / build anyway" design (but unwired), the `PlanSheet` "Continue anyway" for blocked lanes, and the model-studio budget (warn then fail).
- **Hard refusals that are only gameplay or perf choices (best SOFTEN targets):**
  - The `NxPerfCore` clamps (radius 64, per-tick 256, spawns 50 a second, and so on) and the 48 radius default.
  - The `FN_LIMITS` perf caps and the worldgen `maxCost` 100, attempts, counts and template size.
  - The sound counts, per-role durations and the 60 s and 120 s totals.
  - The texture op, size and palette counts.
  - The stress-fail Install block.
  - The perf-watch auto-disable default.
  - The `prompts.js` "build the bounded version and say so" instruction and the "hard rule 10" wording.
- **Keep hard:** command allowlist and injection checks, the net policy, zip, upload, request and body size limits, plan-tier and token or spend gates, the licence gate on the sound library, parser and doc size caps in the model studio, the version registry's pack-format correctness, and the structural worldgen errors.
